Count sequences or lines in a FASTA/FASTQ file

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
count_reads.Rd

Counts the number of sequences in a FASTA or FASTQ file. On Linux-like systems, shell commands are used for faster counting when fast_count = TRUE. On other systems, the file is read in chunks using readLines().

Usage

count_reads(files, file_type = "fastq", chunk_lines = 1e+05, fast_count = TRUE)

Arguments

files

Character vector giving the paths to the input files.

file_type

Character string specifying the file format. Supported values are "fastq" and "fasta". Other values cause the function to return the number of lines in the file.

chunk_lines

Integer specifying the maximum number of lines to read at a time when using the non-Linux code path. Defaults to 1e5.

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used in all operating systems.

Value

An integer vector giving the number of sequences for the input FASTA and FASTQ files, or the total number of lines for unsupported file_type values.

Details

Compressed files with .gz, .bz, or .gz2 extensions are supported. ZIP-compressed files are not supported.

For FASTA files, sequences are identified by lines beginning with ">". For FASTQ files, the number of sequences is calculated as the number of lines divided by four.

If file_type is neither "fasta" nor "fastq", the function returns the total number of lines in the file and prints a message.

ZIP-compressed files (files ending in .zip) are not supported and cause the function to stop with an error.

On Linux-like systems, compressed FASTQ files are counted using zcat and wc, while compressed FASTA files are counted by counting header lines beginning with ">". For uncompressed files, wc and grep are used.

On non-Linux systems, or when fast_count = FALSE, files are read incrementally in chunks to avoid loading the entire file into memory. Setting chunk_lines too high increases memory usage and may slow down the function. Setting it too low can also reduce performance due to the increased number of read operations. FASTQ files are expected to contain exactly four lines per sequence. A warning is issued if the total number of lines is not divisible by four.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Count reads in a FASTQ file
count_reads("reads.fastq", file_type = "fastq")

# Count sequences in a FASTA file
count_reads("sequences.fasta", file_type = "fasta")
} # }
